_note: Few-shot training examples for OKAPI AI guide injection. 'steps' are injected as a hint when the query matches. Fill in or correct element IDs and descriptions. skipInteraction=false means the guide waits for the user to interact with the element before advancing. Restart not needed — file reloads on every request.

steps.title: Measurement Modes
steps.description: Easy OKAPI has 3 modes: Kinetics (time-series), Point (single time-point), and Calibrate (standard curve creation). We start in Kinetics mode.

steps.title: Colorimeter Control Panel
steps.description: This panel controls data recording from your PyBadge colorimeter. In this tutorial we will use sample data instead of a live device.

steps.title: Start Recording
steps.description: This button starts live absorbance recording from the colorimeter. For now, just note its location — we will use a sample file next.

steps.title: Measurement Duration
steps.description: Set how long each recording lasts. 'Infinite' records until you click Stop.

steps.title: Sampling Interval
steps.description: Set the time between each reading. 0 fetches data as fast as available.

steps.title: Load Sample Data
steps.description: Select a kinetics CSV file to explore the app. Sample files are available in the sample_data folder — pick any to continue.

steps.title: Data Chart
steps.description: Your measurement data is visualised here as a time-series chart showing absorbance over time.

steps.title: Select Source to Export
steps.description: Choose which measurement source (channel) to export for calibration.

steps.title: Enter Concentration & Export
steps.description: Enter the known analyte concentration as the reference point, set a file name, and click 'Export Data' to create a calibration CSV.

steps.title: Browse to Saving Location
steps.description: Navigate to the directory where the calibration CSV was just saved so you can select it in the next step.

steps.title: Select the Calibration CSV
steps.description: Find the calibration CSV you exported. Click 'Edit' to verify its contents, then select it.

steps.title: Switch to Calibrate Mode
steps.description: Switch to Calibrate mode to set up the regression and generate the standard curve coefficients.

steps.title: Select Kinetics Quantity
steps.description: Choose which kinetics quantity (maxRate, Slope, Sat, or Time to Sat) to use for the calibration curve.

steps.title: Choose Regression Algorithm
steps.description: Select the fitting algorithm for your standard curve: linear, polynomial, logarithmic, exponential, or Michaelis-Menten.

steps.title: Export Coefficients
steps.description: Enter a name and click 'Export Coefficients' to save the standard curve as a calibration JSON file.

steps.title: Return to Kinetics Mode
steps.description: Switch back to Kinetics mode to apply the calibration to your sample measurements.

steps.title: Select Calibration JSON
steps.description: Select the calibration JSON you just exported here. The standard curve is now applied — concentration will be calculated automatically from your kinetics data.

steps.title: Measurement Mode
steps.description: Find the Measurement Mode selector here. Click to select 'Calibrate'.

steps.title: Measurement Mode
steps.description: Find the Measurement Mode selector here. Click to select 'Kinetics'.

steps.title: Measurement Mode
steps.description: Find the Measurement Mode selector here. Click to select 'Point'.

steps.title: Start Measurement
steps.description: Click this button to begin recording data from the colorimeter. Make sure the device is connected first.

steps.title: Stop Measurement
steps.description: Click this button to stop the recording process manually.

steps.title: File Selection
steps.description: Select a CSV data file to analyze here. Click to open the file picker.

steps.title: Directory Browser
steps.description: Browse and navigate to the directory containing your data files.

steps.title: Calibration JSON
steps.description: Select a calibration standard curve JSON file here to apply concentration conversion.

steps.title: Timeout Control
steps.description: Set the duration for each measurement recording here. Set to Infinite to record until manually stopped.

steps.title: Interval Control
steps.description: Set the time interval between measurement readings. Set to 0 to fetch data as fast as available.

steps.title: Export Analysis
steps.description: Export your analysis results here. Set a reference point, enter a file name, and click Export Data.

steps.title: Select Files to Merge
steps.description: First select the CSV files you want to merge from the file list.

steps.title: Merge CSV Files
steps.description: Click here to combine two CSV files into a single multi-source file.

steps.title: Export Data to Report
steps.description: Click 'Export Data to Report' here to save this analysis snapshot into a named report subject for later compilation.

steps.title: Chart View
steps.description: Your measurement data is visualized as a chart here.

steps.title: Regression Algorithm
steps.description: Choose the regression algorithm for your standard curve: linear, polynomial, logarithmic, exponential, or Michaelis-Menten.

steps.title: Export Coefficients
steps.description: Enter a file name and click Export Coefficients to save your standard curve data as a JSON file.

steps.title: R² Threshold
steps.description: Set the minimum accepted R² value here. Fits below this threshold will not be exported.

steps.title: Window Size
steps.description: Configure the sliding window size for max rate regression. Minimum is 3 data points.

steps.title: Select Time Point
steps.description: Choose which time point to use for point-mode calibration.

steps.title: Measurement Log
steps.description: Real-time log of the measurement recording process. Useful for troubleshooting device connection issues.

steps.title: Switch to Calibrate Mode
steps.description: Select 'Calibrate' from the Measurement Mode selector to enter calibration mode.

steps.title: Select Kinetics Calibration
steps.description: In the calibration type selector, choose 'Kinetics'.

steps.title: Select Data File
steps.description: Select the exported kinetics CSV file containing concentration and kinetic parameters.

steps.title: Select Quantity
steps.description: Choose which kinetic quantity to use for calibration: maxRate, Slope, Sat, or Time to Sat.

steps.title: Choose Regression
steps.description: Select a regression algorithm to fit your standard curve.

steps.title: Export Coefficients
steps.description: Enter a name and export the standard curve coefficients as a JSON file.

steps.title: Switch to Calibrate Mode
steps.description: Select 'Calibrate' from the Measurement Mode selector.

steps.title: Select Point Calibration
steps.description: In the calibration type selector, choose 'Point'.

steps.title: Select Data File
steps.description: Select the exported point CSV file containing concentration and absorbance values.

steps.title: Select Time Point
steps.description: Choose the time point to use for your standard curve.

steps.title: Choose Regression
steps.description: Select a regression algorithm to fit your standard curve.

steps.title: Export Coefficients
steps.description: Enter a name and export the standard curve coefficients as a JSON file.

steps.title: Select Calibration File
steps.description: Select a standard curve JSON file here. This applies the regression coefficients used to convert your kinetics measurements into analyte concentration.

steps.title: Select Data File
steps.description: Choose the kinetics CSV data file you want to analyse.

steps.title: Calibration Curve Details
steps.description: The loaded standard curve coefficients are shown here (top right). This is the model used to convert absorbance / kinetics quantities into concentration.

steps.title: Concentration Value
steps.description: The analyte concentration calculated from your measurement data and the selected standard curve is displayed here.

steps.title: Select Calibration File
steps.description: Select a standard curve JSON file here. This applies the regression coefficients used to convert your point measurement absorbance into analyte concentration.

steps.title: Select Data File
steps.description: Choose the point CSV data file you want to analyse.

steps.title: Calibration Curve Details
steps.description: The loaded standard curve coefficients are shown here (top right). This is the model used to convert absorbance into concentration.

steps.title: Concentration Value
steps.description: The analyte concentration calculated from your point measurement and the selected standard curve is displayed here.

steps.title: Switch to Kinetics or Point Mode
steps.description: Concentration calculation from a sample requires Kinetics or Point measurement mode. Switch to one of those modes here first.

steps.title: Select Calibration File
steps.description: After switching mode, select a standard curve JSON file here to apply the calibration coefficients.

steps.title: Select Data File
steps.description: Choose the CSV data file you want to analyse.

steps.title: Calibration Curve Details
steps.description: Once a calibration file is loaded, its standard curve coefficients are shown here at the top right.

steps.title: Concentration Value
steps.description: The calculated analyte concentration derived from your data and the standard curve is displayed here.

steps.title: Confirm Kinetics Mode
steps.description: Make sure Kinetics mode is selected here before starting.

steps.title: Select Measurement File
steps.description: Select a kinetics measurement CSV file containing the sample data you want to use for calibration.

steps.title: Select Source
steps.description: Choose the measurement source (channel) you want to export for the calibration curve.

steps.title: Enter Concentration & Export
steps.description: Enter the known analyte concentration as the reference point, set a file name, and click 'Export Data' to save a calibration CSV.

steps.title: Browse to Saving Location
steps.description: Navigate to the directory where the calibration CSV was just saved so you can find and select it.

steps.description: Find the calibration CSV you just exported. Click 'Edit' on it to verify its contents, then select it.

steps.title: Switch to Calibrate Mode

steps.title: Choose Regression Algorithm
steps.description: Select the fitting algorithm for your standard curve: linear, polynomial, logarithmic, exponential, or Michaelis-Menten.

steps.title: Export Coefficients
